soil bacterial community structure and function were resilient to changes in rainfall along a steep gradient, and the composition of soil bacterial communities was related to their functional responses to moisture in these rainfall environments.

soil bacterial communities were highly resistant to changes in rainfall environment, and that the composition of bacterial communities was an important determinant of soil respiration responses to moisture.

the composition of soil bacterial communities was an important predictor for how the functional response of the community to moisture changed with rainfall, but that changes in community composition were limited by dispersal constraints and ecological specialization of taxa.

how the structure and function soil bacterial communities respond to altered precipitation.
the mechanisms that underlie community responses to environmental changes, and how the composition of the community affects the ecosystem function.

microbial community composition is a key factor determining the sensitivity of ecosystem function to environmental change.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the composition of soil bacterial communities was an important predictor in how soil respiration responded to changes in rainfall, and that the high compositional resilience of bacterial communities in our study system dictated respiration responses in these treatments.

the ecological mechanisms that determine how soil bacterial communities respond to rainfall are not well understood and that more work is needed to understand how soil bacterial communities may respond to future climate change.
